lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Personal details such as date of birth and nationality should be left off the résumé.
items.because: They are not normally part of hiring evaluation, can introduce irrelevant or legally sensitive considerations, and use scarce header space.

items.says: The triage achievement is repeated in two places with inconsistent reduction figures.
items.because: The same 800+ sensor-signal result is assigned to both the internship and the evaluation-framework project with reductions of 68% and two-thirds.

items.says: The dates leave a 10-month period with no listed study or work between the B.S. and the Junior Software Engineer role.
items.because: The unexplained gap may make a reader wonder whether there was unemployment, further education, or an omitted role.

items.says: The diagnostic-accuracy improvement does not identify its baseline or evaluation set.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the 35% represents, what it was compared against, or whether it was measured on a held-out set.

items.says: Assistant-only loss masking does not by itself make a model reproduce tool outputs more faithfully.
items.because: It normally excludes tool-result tokens from the loss and trains assistant responses conditioned on those results rather than direct reproduction of them.

items.says: The bullet states the intended training behavior rather than the result achieved.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the intervention worked or why it mattered to the system.

items.says: The 68% backlog reduction is attributed to the triage branch based only on a post-launch before-and-after change.
items.because: Case inflow, staffing, policy, process changes, or the backlog definition could also explain the reduction.

items.says: The same adapter fine-tuning achievement is repeated in two bullets.
items.because: Both bullets describe assistant-only loss masking on the same adapter, making the work appear duplicated and potentially padded.

items.says: Switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision alone does not support a 4x reduction in total fine-tuning GPU memory.
items.because: BF16 usually halves eligible tensor storage while mixed-precision training commonly retains FP32 master weights, optimizer states, and other buffers.

items.says: The GPU-memory reduction is not connected to what it enabled.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether it enabled larger models, longer sequences, more examples, or lower infrastructure cost.

items.says: The regression checks are described in the present tense inside an otherwise past-tense bullet.
items.because: “Adds” interrupts the historical framing established by “Maintained” and “shortened.”

items.says: The release-cycle bullet gives the endpoint but not the starting point.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether reaching three days was a major improvement or a marginal change.

items.says: The bullet does not quantify the nightly backlog or dispatch delay.
items.because: A reader cannot judge the scale of the operational problem or the benefit to morning dispatch.

items.says: The claim that AI-first practices were adopted across the platform and improved delivery and downstream outcomes is not established by the line.
items.because: It gives no concrete practices, adoption coverage, delivery comparison, or downstream outcome evidence.

items.says: The context-size bullet does not show what capability the bounded context enabled or the achieved value below 10K tokens.
items.because: “Working context” is ambiguous, and the reader cannot tell the actual peak, whether needed information was retained, or what user-facing benefit resulted.

items.says: Separating concurrency pools and gating cache writes cannot by itself support the unqualified claim that the changes removed deadlocks and lost tool results.
items.because: Other locks, queues, limits, cancellation, retries, fan-in, or crashes can still cause failures, so bounded test conditions or reliability evidence are needed.

items.says: “Under 50-way fan-out” gives the test scale but not the size or consistency of the reliability improvement.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether failures were consistently eliminated or merely observed less often.

items.says: “Removing lost tool results” is grammatically awkward.
items.because: Lost results are prevented from being lost, not removed.

items.says: The evaluation-module contribution does not state what changed as a result.
items.because: The metric count shows scope but not an improvement in evaluation coverage, defect detection, or adoption.

items.says: The integration description does not show how it was implemented.
items.because: A technical reader cannot tell whether the work involved an interface, abstraction, pipeline, or another reusable mechanism.

items.says: “Showed the evaluator tracks” is grammatically incorrect and overstates what the correlation establishes.
items.because: The clause needs “that,” conflicts with the past-tense framing, and treats a strong monotonic association under tested conditions as broad evaluator validity.

items.says: The bullet does not identify which evaluator output was correlated with which degradation measure, and “injected degradation” is compressed jargon.
items.because: A reader cannot interpret what the 0.89 measures or easily understand the test design.

items.says: The final bullet misattributes the industrial-inspection backlog result to the evaluation-framework project.
items.because: Nothing in the project entry connects the evaluation framework to the industrial inspection system, sensor workflow, or operational backlog.

items.says: The final bullet changes subject from the evaluation framework to the internship’s diagnostics work.
items.because: The unrelated triage bullet breaks the project narrative and weakens confidence that the work belongs to this entry.
